GENERAL SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating ? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

4. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.

7. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Reproduction? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Reproduction.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Human Reproduction.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Reproduction.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Reproduction.

9. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts ? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Heating effect of current ● Experiments on heating effect of current ● Factors d and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Human Reproduction and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
